objectives.statement: Use geographical vocabulary and a labelled sketch to compare coastal and inland landscapes in Liberia.

blocks.instructionalPurpose: Sustained reading with words explained in context. Learner action: Read or listen, make a labelled sketch and ask one question about a place you know.

accessibility.textAlternative: Reading Liberia's landscape. Liberia lies in West Africa beside the Atlantic Ocean. Coastal means near the sea. Inland means farther from the coast. Liberia has coastal lowlands, with hills and higher land farther inland. These broad descriptions do not give every place the same shape. A plain is a broad area of fairly level land. A plateau is higher land with a fairly level surface. A physical region describes landscape features. It is not the same as a county boundary. Read a map's key before using its symbols.

blocks.instructionalPurpose: Sustained reading with words explained in context. Learner action: Select two relevant details, explain their different meanings and name one missing observation.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two invented reading-club records. These reading clubs and observations are invented for this lesson. Club A is near the coast. Its covered room stayed dry during two observed showers. Water covered part of its path during one shower. Nobody checked the path after dark. Club B is inland beside a river. Its room had a leaking roof. Its path stayed clear during both observed showers. Nobody checked the river after prolonged rain. Both clubs want books kept dry and a route that an adult can check.

blocks.instructionalPurpose: Diagnose a worked attempt that contains a common misconception. Learner action: Identify the faulty reason and propose a condition for a defensible recommendation.

responseSignals.feedback: Reversing the preference still uses a region label instead of local evidence.
The room and route are separate needs. Evidence about one does not settle the other.

accessibility.textAlternative: A club needs dry book storage and a route an adult can check. A fictional pupil wrote: Club B is inland. Therefore its room and path must meet every need. Which response best repairs the reasoning? Options: Use the roof and route observations, then name a repair or further check.; Choose Club A just because it is coastal instead.; Ignore the roof because the path was clear..
